rows.reason: One snapshot is threaded through TX_RING reservation, frame copy sizing and tpacket_fill_skb. LL_RESERVED_SPACE_EX consumes the explicit length without changing other callers of the original macro. Both changed implementation functions belong to targeted af_packet; no broad header caller substitution is required for this CVE. The separate DGRAM/header_ops issue remains outside upstream fix scope.
The replacement removal path clears the cached new transport before queuing a heartbeat can reuse a removed peer. No object layout change or external module inline repair is required.

Both halves of the primary correction are present in sctp: cleared cached ASCONF and safe late timer expiry. Accepting only the free-pointer half would leave the newly exposed timer NULL race; this payload covers it.

The moved gap-acked chunk is rebound at the primary list move. An additional livepatch-side consistency repair in sctp_check_transmitted also reconciles a mismatched retained transport before later accounting. Both paths compile into the targeted sctp object; no layout substitution.
The removal replacement scrubs control_chunk_list as well as the existing data list. This is the missing primary control-reply pointer cleanup in the targeted sctp object.

The module replacement includes the parsed header descriptor, one-time IPv4 length checks, writable-length bounds and both input/output callers of the changed helper signature. Core/xmit and inline parser code are compiled inside ip_vs, an explicit target. A commit in the backport graph alone would not prove this.

The IPVS tunnel error replacement clears the stale options immediately after packet/network-header rebase, keeping the rest of the control block and ingress context. The complete affected helper is in targeted ip_vs.

The replacement pairs RCU-protected walking with a new helper holding the existing fnhe_lock for the MTU/locked pair. Both implementation files are built into targeted vmlinux. The added header item is a prototype for this explicit changed caller, not a behavior change needing unrelated callers to be rebuilt.

The module replacement contains the upstream missing-running check and additional synchronous timer cleanup in uninit for previously armed devices. Both changed methods belong to targeted vxlan; no device structure-layout change.

The error function clears cloned IPv6 control metadata before the pull/rebase and icmpv6_send. Exact archived boot CONFIG_IPV6_TUNNEL=y places this function in targeted vmlinux; no absent ip6_tunnel module protection is assumed. MIP6 type/state availability remains conditional reachability, independent of correction content.

Primary getter correction is present and forced inline. Core multicast caller under targeted vmlinux is covered in source. However v6 uses an explicit subset of module targets; a complete affected-inline-caller/replacement inventory is not yet proved. Later v7 source explicitly treats header fanout as unbounded and removes the target list. No unconditional accepted tuple until that exact v6 fanout scope is resolved.
rows.architect_disposition: Final conservative partial coverage; whole-CVE mitigation uses later fixed kernel

earlier_modules: Observed versions2–5 precede the first-v6 corrections in canonical coverage; not accepted for these11. Their identity dispositions are separately central, not mistaken for source-content acceptance.
activation_contract: Content acceptance permits only exact reviewed tuples. Existing evaluator alone decides loaded/enabled/stable state, boot continuity, counterpart transitions and mitigation timestamp. Quarantine is deployment risk, not denial of historical content.
limits: No new kernel/module build, exploit or API call
Ten decisions are source replacement/target review, not binary symbol or transition execution tests
74630 has a material header-fanout completeness gap; leave unaccepted until resolved
No per-node safe history override or manual evaluation edit
architect_74630_decision: Whole-v6 tuples withheld absent exact fanout replacement proof; known partial source correction retained, later fixed-kernel boundary accepted as conservative. No source-default safety or absent-protection assertion.
